title: MOE answers questions on Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying
asked: MPs asked about the Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying, including guidelines for class or school transfers, caning, cyberbullying, reporting channels, counselling resources, effectiveness measures, transparency, workload, consistency, and support for victims.
asked_by: Mr Alex Yeo and other Members
answered_by: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
response: The Minister said MOE completed the Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying and announced recommendations on 15 April, spanning four key areas and nine measures. He outlined measures including values education, school culture, school capacity, and partnerships, with an online reporting platform from 2027, clearer disciplinary guidelines, and caning only for boys and egregious violations. He also cited baseline bullying incidence data and said MOE will provide needs-based funding for additional manpower and explore technology to streamline case management.

key_points.point: MOE completed the Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying and announced recommendations on 15 April this year, spanning four key areas and nine measures.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: completed the Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying and announced the recommendations on 15 April this year

key_points.point: From 2027, each school will have an online reporting platform for students and parents.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: From 2027, each school will have an online reporting platform available for students and parents.

key_points.point: Bullying incidents in the last five years averaged three per 1,000 primary school students and eight per 1,000 secondary school students per year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: bullying incidents in the last five years averaged three incidents per 1,000 in our primary school students and eight per 1,000 secondary school students per year

key_points.point: Caning is for boys only and only for egregious violations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: Caning is meted out for boys only and, as I said earlier, only for egregious violations.

key_points.point: Caning must be approved by the Principal and administered only by authorised teachers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: caning must be approved by the Principal and administered only by authorised teachers

key_points.point: All schools will develop an anti-bullying policy by the end of this year based on MOE's guidelines.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: All schools will also develop an anti-bullying policy by the end of this year that is based on MOE's guidelines.

key_points.point: MOE will provide needs-based funding for schools to hire additional manpower or services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: MOE will, therefore, provide funding for our schools, on a needs-basis, to hire additional manpower or services

key_points.point: The Online Safety Commission will become operational by the end of next month, June 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: When the Online Safety Commission (OSC) becomes operational by the end of next month, June 2026

key_points.point: MOE is developing an offence management system to support case investigation, documentation and monitoring.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: MOE is developing an offence management system to support case investigation, documentation and monitoring.

left_open: How schools assess whether restorative actions such as relationship repair are successful before allowing affected students to continue in the same learning environment.
Whether studies have been conducted to assess if current counselling resources in schools are sufficient.
Whether school counsellors are sufficiently equipped to deal with fast-evolving challenges of online bullying.
What specific indicators and evaluation methodology MOE will use to assess effectiveness and consistency of schools' implementation.
Whether the Ministry currently tracks longitudinal outcomes such as the proportion of students who reoffend after a first serious bullying incident.
Whether the distinctions in caning application, including between boys and girls and commencement only from upper primary levels, are based on established research.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered fairness and escalation, cyberbullying thresholds, caning consistency, reporting volume, transparency, and victim support.
